result: Epithelial-specific knockout of Invs in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mice leads to progressive renal cystic disease with kidney enlargement beginning at P14, cyst formation primarily in collecting ducts and thick ascending limbs (but not proximal tubules), and progressive kidney function decline as measured by BUN levels.
evaluation: Claims C3, C21-C37, and C124 collectively demonstrate a well-characterized progressive phenotype with detailed time-course data (P7, P14, P21, P28) showing kidney enlargement, cyst formation in specific nephron segments, and functional decline. The data include morphological assessments, immunofluorescence, histology, and functional measurements (BUN), providing converging evidence for the progressive cystic disease phenotype.

result: Stromal-specific knockout of Invs in Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice shows no observable renal phenotypes up to 8 weeks of age, despite effective deletion of Invs in stromal cells as demonstrated by reduced INVS and ANKS6 localization to cilia in cultured interstitial cells.
evaluation: Claims C4, C51, C53-C60 demonstrate absence of phenotypes at P28 and P56 with multiple measurements (kidney size, KBW ratio, cyst formation, collagen deposition, SMA, BUN). Effective deletion is validated by reduced INVS (85% to 34%) and ANKS6 (88% to 40%) positive cilia in cultured interstitial cells (C56-C59), confirming the negative result is not due to failed deletion.

result: Myofibroblast activation and fibrotic response precede detectable cyst formation in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidneys, with increased SMA and vimentin expression detected at P7 before cysts are visible, suggesting fibrosis is triggered independently of cyst formation.
evaluation: Claims C5, C38-C45, and C99 provide temporal evidence showing increased fibrotic markers (SMA, vimentin) at P7 when no cysts are detected (C25, C44, C45), with progressive increases at P9, P14, P21, and P28. Both immunostaining and RT-qPCR data support early fibrotic response. The inference that fibrosis precedes cyst formation is well-supported by the temporal sequence.

result: Cell proliferation is abnormally increased in both collecting duct epithelial cells and interstitial cells at P7 in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidneys, before detectable cyst formation, as measured by PCNA and pHH3 staining.
evaluation: Claims C46-C49 demonstrate increased proliferation in both epithelial and interstitial compartments at P7 using multiple markers (PCNA for S-phase and interphase, pHH3 for mitosis). The data show significant increases in both cell types with proper quantification methods, supporting both cell-autonomous and non-autonomous proliferation effects.

result: Genetic removal of cilia by Ift88 deletion partially suppresses the renal cystic disease, fibrosis, and kidney function decline in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants, suggesting INVS functions to inhibit a cilia-dependent pro-cystic and pro-fibrotic pathway similar to polycystins.
evaluation: Claims C6, C64-C76, C105-C106, and C116 demonstrate that Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutants show reduced severity compared to Invs single mutants across multiple parameters (KBW ratio, cystic index, BUN, SMA, vimentin, collagen I) at P21. The data confirm cilia are present in Invs mutants (C64-C65) but absent in double mutants (C66), establishing the genetic epistasis relationship. Statistical comparisons show significant partial rescue.

result: Ift88 deletion reduces the abnormally increased cell proliferation in both collecting duct and interstitial cells of Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants at P21, as measured by PCNA immunostaining and Western blot analysis of proliferation markers (PCNA, CDK1, cyclin D1).
evaluation: Claims C77-C87 provide quantitative data showing Ift88 deletion reduces PCNA-positive cells in both epithelial (22.9% to 13.4%) and interstitial (22.3% to 12.8%) compartments in Invs mutants. Western blot data confirm reduced levels of PCNA, CDK1, and cyclin D1 in double mutants compared to Invs single mutants, providing converging evidence for reduced proliferation.

result: INVS is not required for ciliary localization of PC2 in mIMCD3 cells, as demonstrated by immunostaining of Invs-/- CRISPR knockout cell lines.
evaluation: Claim C88 is supported by immunostaining data from two independent Invs-/- clones (CR81 and CR84) showing no difference in PC2 ciliary localization compared to controls (Figure 6E and F). This provides mechanistic insight that INVS function is independent of PC2 localization.

result: VPA treatment reduces cyst burden, decreases cell proliferation, ameliorates kidney function decline, and reduces myofibroblast activation in Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mutant mice, suggesting VPA as a potential therapeutic candidate for NPHP.
evaluation: Claims C7, C90-C97, C112, and C118 demonstrate VPA treatment (200 mg/kg IP daily from P10-P28) significantly reduces multiple disease parameters (kidney size, KBW ratio, cystic index, BUN, SMA, PCNA-positive cells, proliferation markers) in mutants while having no significant effect on controls (C94), suggesting selective therapeutic benefit. The data include morphological, functional, and molecular measurements providing comprehensive evidence.

result: Defective epithelial cells are the main driver of NPHP phenotypes in Invs mutants, with epithelial-stromal crosstalk playing a significant role in the development of interstitial fibrosis.
evaluation: Claims C98 and C115 represent conclusions drawn from the comparison of epithelial-specific (Cdh16-Cre) and stromal-specific (Foxd1-Cre) knockout models. The severe phenotypes in epithelial knockouts (C3) and absence of phenotypes in stromal knockouts (C4) provide strong evidence for this conclusion. The early increase in interstitial cell proliferation (C47) and fibrotic markers (C5) in epithelial mutants further supports epithelial-stromal crosstalk.

result: Renal epithelial cilia play a critical role in NPHP pathogenesis.
evaluation: Claim C117 is a conclusion supported by the genetic epistasis experiments showing that removal of cilia (Ift88 deletion) partially suppresses Invs mutant phenotypes (C6, C71-C76, C80, C84, C87), demonstrating that intact cilia are required for full manifestation of disease. This is a major conceptual conclusion of the study.

result: Background knowledge and prior work establishing the context for the study, including information about cilia function, ciliopathies, NPHP genetics, INVS localization and function, polycystin function, and existing therapeutic approaches.
evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C8-C20, C50, C61-C63, C89, C101-C104, C107-C111, C113-C114, C120-C123 represent established knowledge from prior work, properly cited throughout the manuscript. These provide essential context but are not novel findings of this study.

result: A proposed model that INVS functions to signal terminal differentiation of renal epithelial cells and Invs mutant cells fail to exit cell cycle to enter quiescence.
evaluation: Claim C100 is explicitly stated as a speculative model ('An attractive model is...') to explain the observed proliferation phenotype. While the increased proliferation data (C46-C49, C77-C87) are well-supported, this specific mechanistic model about terminal differentiation signaling is not directly tested and remains speculative.

result: The reduction of body weight at P28 in Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mice is more moderate than in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mice.
evaluation: Claim C119 is supported by comparative data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 showing body weight reduction is less severe in Pkhd1-Cre mutants compared to Cdh16-Cre mutants. This is consistent with the later onset of Pkhd1-Cre expression (E14.5 vs E11.5, C89) and provides rationale for using the Pkhd1-Cre model for drug treatment studies.
